Case Title: A child with fever and joint pain who turned out not to have the common cause
Case Type: Rare presentation of a common disease
Presenting Complaint & History: A child presented with three weeks of intermittent fever and left knee swelling, initially treated as presumed reactive arthritis at a local clinic without improvement.
Clinical & Social Context: The family lives roughly two hours from the nearest health centre with reliable transport; the delay in presentation reflected genuine access barriers rather than reluctance.
Examination & Investigation Findings: Knee effusion with reduced range of motion; chest X-ray incidentally showed a calcified focus; joint fluid analysis was suggestive of tuberculous arthritis.
Diagnosis: Skeletal (joint) tuberculosis, an uncommon presentation of a common regional disease.
Management / Intervention: Anti-tubercular therapy initiated per weight-band dosing; joint immobilization and physiotherapy referral arranged.
Outcome & Follow-up Detail: Symptoms resolved over 8 weeks of therapy; full range of motion recovered by 4 months; treatment completed under directly observed therapy.
Discussion / Learning Point: Joint tuberculosis should stay on the differential for non-resolving monoarticular swelling in TB-endemic areas, even without classic pulmonary symptoms.

Case Title: A social story: the cost of a referral
Presenting Complaint & History: A man in his 40s presented with escalating abdominal pain that ultimately required referral to a facility 90 km away for surgical evaluation.
Clinical & Social Context: The referral was medically straightforward, but the case highlighted how out-of-pocket transport and lost wages nearly caused the family to decline it.
Examination & Investigation Findings: Findings consistent with a surgical abdomen; point-of-care ultrasound supported the need for higher-level care.
Diagnosis: Underlying diagnosis confirmed after referral (acute cholecystitis); the point of this case is the pathway, not the pathology.
Management / Intervention: Facilitated referral with transport arranged through a local support scheme; case used to advocate for a standing transport-assistance fund.
Outcome & Follow-up Detail: Patient underwent successful surgery after a two-day delay caused by arranging funds.
Discussion / Learning Point: Clinical management is often the easy part; the systemic barrier to acting on it is where rural care actually succeeds or fails, and where policy intervention has the most leverage.
Patient / Family Perspective: "We would have waited until it was an emergency if the community fund hadn't existed."

Case Title: An adolescent with an unusual skin presentation
Presenting Complaint & History: An adolescent presented with a slowly progressive pigmented skin lesion present for over a year, previously dismissed as a fungal infection by multiple providers.
Clinical & Social Context: Limited access to dermatology expertise locally meant the lesion went unbiopsied for over a year despite repeated visits.
Examination & Investigation Findings: Biopsy after referral showed features consistent with a rare cutaneous condition; multidisciplinary opinion sought.
Diagnosis: A rare dermatological diagnosis, still being confirmed with specialist input at time of writing.
Management / Intervention: Referred to tertiary dermatology; topical management initiated pending confirmation.
Outcome & Follow-up Detail: Follow-up ongoing; case will be updated once the diagnostic workup is complete.
Discussion / Learning Point: A one-year diagnostic delay for a visible lesion illustrates a gap in access to basic dermatology referral pathways in this setting, worth flagging for the district health plan.
